newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon doubts impact of new HK airport on Cathay.
newsitem.headline: Salomon doubts impact of new HK airport on Cathay.

text.p: The higher cost of Hong Kong's new airport is likely to have only a small impact on the 1998 earnings of Cathay Pacific 0293.HK, Salomon Brothers said in a report which left its previous Hold rating for Cathay unchanged.
Salomon said increases in capacity should "almost offset" increased landing charges at Chek Lap Kok.

This would contradict recent statements by Cathay executives on the controversial new fee structure that the carrier will be worst hit by higher user charges and unprofitable routes would have to be cut.

The new structure has not yet been announced by the Airport Authority which has denied claims by the airline's representative body, the International Air Transport Association, and other users groups that the new airport will become one of the world's most expensive.
Salomon's Hong Kong based aviation analyst, Peter Negline, said increased charges may not have as big an impact as feared because of increased capacity.
Negline's report said landing charges will double from Kai Tak but the new 24 hour, twin rnnways at Chek Lap Kok will allow a substantial boost to available landing slots.

After the new airport opens, Cathay is due to take delivery of new aircraft which should result in a 14.2 per cent increase in available seat capacity in 1998 instead of 10.3 per cent as first estimated.

"In addition, the delayed return of two Boeing 747-400's on operating lease from 1998/9 to 2002/3 should result in an increase in available seat capacity in 1999 of 4.2 per cent against our previous estimate of 2.4 per cent," the report said.

"We believe these increases in capacity should provide enough incremental revenue to almost offset the higher landing charges. We further believe that the airport will prove to be a major boon for Hong Kong and that Cathay is likely to be the largest individual beneficiary, behind the people of Hong Kong, of course," the report added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
